question: Can archived target-board photos establish VD3 cathode lead and its copper net?

source_schematic.reading: VD3 cathode is at the R66.2/R67.1 junction (SOUND_CLAMP); anode is at ground.

component_views.observation: The vertical glass diode sits between R67 and R66. A dark circumferential band appears near its upper end, consistent with a cathode mark, but the adjacent raised lead and lacquer hide a unique net chase.
Independent oblique view shows the same installed diode and upper dark band; it does not expose a soldered copper endpoint.

solder_view.transform: D102-local board-to-component inverse followed by component-to-solder affine; these are model-pad projections, not identified physical solder joints
solder_view.observation: The projected sites lie among backside copper and holes, but the component-side diode leads are raised/lap-soldered and no matching VD3 through-hole annulus is identifiable. Nearby backside copper cannot establish either diode lead net.

model_state.pin_names: generic D_DIODE labels 1=K and 2=A, contradicting exact .009 schematic polarity
model_state.disposition: Value/placement retained. Do not claim polarity or remap pad numbers until cathode-band lead and continuity to R66.2/R67.1 and ground are both established.
